newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends sharply up on hot and dry forecasts.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends sharply up on hot and dry forecasts.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed sharply higher on forecasts for hotter and drier weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
"The market is concerned about some heat and there will be some stress. But heat of that magnitude next week could bring more serious problems," Dean Witter analyst Jerry Gidel.
Meteorologists Tuesday said a heat wave was expected in the Midwest through Friday.

They said high temperatures would range from the low- to high-90-degrees-Fahrenheit area, beginning Tuesday. Concerns abounded that the weather would harm some of the corn crop which is entering its crucial pollination or reproductive stage.
USDA Monday said seven percent of the U.S. corn crop was silking as of Sunday. Silking is the early stage of pollination.
"The percent of pollination could move from seven percent this week to 20 next week so 80 percent of the crop would yet to be pollinated at the start of next week," Gidel said.
Corn closed four to 8-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July up 8-1/2 at $2.70-3/4. September closed 7-1/2 cents higher at $2.56 and December closed 7-1/2 higher at $2.56-1/2.

Also USDA on Monday reported a deterioration in the condition of the U.S. crop. As of Sunday, USDA said, the corn crop was 73 percent good to excellent, down from 75 percent in that category the previous week.
Traders said the weather concerns and fund short covering were at the heart of Tuesday's rally.

"There was a lot of short covering in corn of 40 million to 50 million bushels or more," Gidel said. "They may have got ahead of the game a little (when corn recently dropped) but they may be getting a little ahead going the other way now."
Funds bought roughly 65 million bushels of corn Tuesday with Merrill Lynch Futures a key buyer of 22.0 million bushels of December and 18.0 million bushels of March, traders said.
Signs of hedge selling surfaced. ADM Investor Services sold five million bushels of September and Term Commodities sold three million bushels of December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 100,000 contracts, above the 87,929 traded Monday.

In corn options, Term Commodities sold 400 September $2.70 calls at 5-1/2 cents, Farmers Commodities Corp bought 225 September $2.60 calls at 10-1/2 cents and Rand Financial sold 300 December $2.50 calls at 18 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 25,000 contracts, below the 28,394 traded Monday.
